title: Grassroots Democracy — Part 2: Local Government in Rural Areas

learn.hook: The village handpump is broken. Who fixes it? The village's own government, the gram panchayat!
points: A gram sabha is made up of all the adults (18 years and above) of a village or group of villages whose names are on the voters' list.
The voters of the gram sabha elect the members of the gram panchayat (panches or ward members). Its head, the sarpanch (also called pradhan or mukhiya in some states), is also elected.
The gram panchayat looks after local needs: drinking water, village roads, drains, streetlights, cleanliness and keeping records like births and deaths.
In gram sabha meetings, villagers discuss plans, approve work and question the panchayat about how money was spent. This keeps the panchayat answerable to the people.
A panchayat secretary, appointed by the government, keeps records and calls meetings. Panchayats get money from local taxes and from government grants.

example.q: Sunita, aged 19, lives in a village and her name is on the voters' list. Can she take part in the gram sabha?
steps: Every adult aged 18 or above on the village voters' list is a member of the gram sabha.
Sunita is 19 and on the list.
So she is a member and can attend and speak.
example.answer: Yes, she is a member of the gram sabha.

learn.reallife: When villages build a new pond, a school toilet or a concrete lane under a government scheme, the gram panchayat usually plans and supervises the work.

quiz.q: Who are the members of the gram sabha?
options: All adults of the village whose names are on the voters' list
quiz.explain: Every adult (18+) on the voters' list of the panchayat area is a member.
quiz.mistake: Confuses the gram sabha with the gram panchayat

quiz.q: What is the head of a gram panchayat usually called?
quiz.explain: The sarpanch (or pradhan or mukhiya) heads the gram panchayat.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up rural and urban leaders

quiz.q: How does a person become a sarpanch?
options: By being appointed by the school principal
By being born into the post
quiz.explain: The sarpanch is elected. In most states villagers vote directly; in a few, the elected panchayat members choose the sarpanch.
quiz.mistake: Thinks the post is appointed or inherited

quiz.q: Which of these is a duty of the gram panchayat?
quiz.explain: Panchayats handle local needs like water, roads, drains and streetlights.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up local and national duties

quiz.q: Why are gram sabha meetings important?
options: Villagers can discuss plans and question the panchayat
quiz.explain: The gram sabha keeps the panchayat answerable to the people.
quiz.mistake: Does not know the role of the gram sabha

quiz.q: Who keeps the records of the gram panchayat and calls its meetings?
quiz.explain: The secretary, appointed by the government, keeps records and calls meetings.
quiz.mistake: Does not know the secretary's role

quiz.q: What is the minimum age to be a member of the gram sabha?
quiz.explain: Every person aged 18 or above whose name is on the voters' list is a member.
quiz.mistake: Confuses the age with another rule

quiz.q: Where does a gram panchayat get money for its work?
options: Local taxes and grants from the government
quiz.explain: Panchayats collect some local taxes and receive grants from state and central governments.
quiz.mistake: Thinks the panchayat has no source of money

teach.ask: Gappu asks, 'Who runs a village? Is there a government even for one village?'
teach.praise: Wow! All adult voters form the gram sabha, and they elect the gram panchayat, led by a sarpanch, to look after the village!
teach.nudge: Who are the members of the gram sabha, and who leads the gram panchayat?

learn.hook: Panchayats are like a three-storey building: the village on the ground floor, the block in the middle and the district on top!
points: Panchayati raj is the system of local self-government in rural areas. It has three tiers (levels).
Tier 1 is the gram panchayat at the village level. Tier 2 is the panchayat samiti (also called block panchayat) at the block level. Tier 3 is the zila parishad at the district level.
The 73rd Amendment to the Constitution, passed in 1992, made panchayati raj a part of the Constitution. It came into force on 24 April 1993, which is why 24 April is National Panchayati Raj Day.
Panchayat elections are held every 5 years and are conducted by the State Election Commission.
At least one-third of the seats in panchayats are reserved for women; many states reserve half. Seats are also reserved for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes.

example.q: A road is needed to join several villages within one block. Which tier would most likely plan it?
steps: A road within one village is the gram panchayat's work.
A road joining many villages of a block is bigger than one village.
So the panchayat samiti, at the block level, would plan it.

learn.reallife: Many women sarpanches across India have led their villages in building toilets, saving water and improving schools, thanks to reserved seats.

items.q: How many tiers does panchayati raj have?
Panchayat elections are held every how many years?
Which amendment set up panchayati raj in the Constitution (number)?
In which year was the 73rd Amendment passed?
National Panchayati Raj Day falls on which date in April?
What fraction of panchayat seats, at least, is reserved for women?

quiz.q: How many tiers does the panchayati raj system have?
quiz.explain: The three tiers are the gram panchayat, panchayat samiti and zila parishad.

quiz.q: At which level does the zila parishad work?
quiz.explain: The zila parishad is the top tier, working at the district level.

quiz.q: What is the middle tier of panchayati raj, at the block level, called?
quiz.explain: The panchayat samiti links the gram panchayats and the zila parishad.
quiz.mistake: Confuses the panchayat samiti with the gram sabha

quiz.q: Which amendment to the Constitution set up the panchayati raj system?
quiz.explain: The 73rd Amendment (1992) is about rural local government; the 74th is about urban local government.

quiz.q: When is National Panchayati Raj Day celebrated?
quiz.explain: The 73rd Amendment came into force on 24 April 1993, so this day is celebrated each year.
quiz.mistake: Confuses it with other national days

quiz.explain: Each state's Election Commission conducts elections to panchayats and municipal bodies.
quiz.mistake: Thinks courts or banks conduct elections

quiz.q: At least what share of panchayat seats is reserved for women?
quiz.explain: The 73rd Amendment reserves at least one-third of seats for women; many states reserve half.
quiz.mistake: Does not know about reservation for women

quiz.q: How often are panchayat elections held?
quiz.explain: Panchayats have a term of five years, after which fresh elections are held.
quiz.mistake: Confuses the term with other periods

teach.ask: Gappu asks, 'Is the gram panchayat all there is for villages, or is there more?'
teach.praise: Ahaa! Panchayati raj has three tiers: gram panchayat for the village, panchayat samiti for the block and zila parishad for the district!
teach.nudge: How many tiers are there, and what are they called at the village, block and district levels?
